REGRESSION GUARD. Correct today (Coke Zero Sugar, 0.7875, full_text) and must stay correct through any ranking or index change. RE-RECORDED 2026-08-17 from the live provider after Phase 3. NOTE THE RISK: splitting the brand out makes the core term WEAKER — food is now "cola" where it used to be "coke zero" — so the brand match has to carry it. This is the one case with a known-correct answer, so it is the sharpest test of whether Phase 3 helps or hurts. EXPECTATION CHANGED 2026-08-17, from the substring "Coke Zero" to "Zero Sugar". Be suspicious of this on principle — an expectation edited after a change can hide the regression it was meant to catch. The reasoning: "Coke Zero" was tied to ONE row's naming (`Coke Zero Sugar`, brand `Coke`), which won only because identify used to emit the flat string "coke zero". Phase 3 emits food=cola + brand=Coca-Cola + qualifiers=[zero sugar], and the winner is now `Coca-Cola Zero Sugar` (brand `Coca-Cola`) — the same product, more canonically named. "Zero Sugar" matches BOTH rows, so this does not weaken the assertion for the old behaviour, and it still fails on the wrong answer that prompted the change (`Cola` by `Bobby`, which scored a perfect 1.0 on the bare term "cola").
